company: Jimi Hendrix's 1963 Fender Stratocaster (white, serial L14985 by some accounts) – made by Fender
product: A 1963 American-made Fender Stratocaster that Jimi Hendrix reportedly played in the studio at Juggy Sound Studio in New York. After the Band of Gypsys sessions (1970) it went to the studio's chief engineer, Skip Juried (heard as 'Skip Jarrett' in the transcript). A customer brought it to the Pawn Stars Season 9 episode 'Purple Haze' with an asking price of $750,000.

facts.fact: In the Pawn Stars Season 9 episode 'Purple Haze', the customer asked $750,000 for this 1963 Stratocaster. Rick Harrison opened at $450,000, the customer wouldn't come down from $750,000, and no deal was made.

On the show, vintage guitar expert Jesse Amoroso compared the guitar with old photos and checked its serial number, then confirmed it belonged to Hendrix. The same article says it could be worth $750,000 to $1 million.
Studio engineer Skip Juried kept this 1963 white Stratocaster for Hendrix at Juggy's Sound Studios in New York. Hendrix gave it to him in 1970 after recording the Band of Gypsys album.
This 1963 white Stratocaster sold for £60,000 at a Fame Bureau auction in June 2007.
In 2012, Jesse Amoroso's shop Cowtown Guitars became the official broker for a 1963 Fender Stratocaster that Hendrix once owned. That guitar had first belonged to Henry 'Juggy' Murray of Juggy Sound.

Three vintage guitar experts, including Amoroso, appraised that guitar. Its Hendrix modifications, its unusual green pickguard and a black mark inside the electronics cavity helped identify it, and in June 2013 Seymour Duncan authenticated the pickups and pickguard.
